title: Beautiful Pairs
statement:
You are given two 0-indexed integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of the same length. A pair of indices (i,j) is called beautiful if|nums1[i] - nums1[j]| + |nums2[i] - nums2[j]| is the smallest amongst all possible indices pairs where i < j.

Return the beautiful pair as [i, j] with i < j. In the case that there are multiple beautiful pairs, return the lexicographically smallest pair.

Note that

- |x| denotes the absolute value of x.
- A pair of indices (i1, j1) is lexicographically smaller than (i2, j2) if i1 < i2 or i1 == i2 and j1 < j2.

## Examples

### Example 1

```text
Input: nums1 = [1,2,3,2,4], nums2 = [2,3,1,2,3]
Output: [0,3]
```

Consider index 0 and index 3. The value of |nums1[i]-nums1[j]| + |nums2[i]-nums2[j]| is 1, which is the smallest value we can achieve.

### Example 2

```text
Input: nums1 = [1,2,4,3,2,5], nums2 = [1,4,2,3,5,1]
Output: [1,4]
```

Consider index 1 and index 4. The value of |nums1[i]-nums1[j]| + |nums2[i]-nums2[j]| is 1, which is the smallest value we can achieve.

## Constraints

- 2 <= nums1.length, nums2.length <= 10^5
- nums1.length == nums2.length
- 0 <= nums1[i] <= nums1.length
- 0 <= nums2[i] <= nums2.length
